issues.failure_explanation: The Introduction asserts that the projection of g* onto ker(I-P) equals the classical long-run average reward vector g, and the appendix section 'justification' promises to show that (v*,g*) recovers g. No formal result in the source establishes this: that section contains only the telescoping return identity (lem:app_telescoping / eq:app_return_decomp_star) and the transient-cost identity (prop:app_vstar_transient_cost). The needed nontrivial argument — that on the semisimple peripheral subspace K(P) the Cesàro averages (1/T)sum_{t<T} P^t converge to the spectral projection onto ker(I-P), giving g = Pi_{ker(I-P)} g* and the coordinate formula g(s) = sum_i bar-theta_i p_i(s) with bar-theta_i the phase-average of the anchor coordinates theta*_{i,k} — is missing. The experiments nevertheless measure Err(t) = ||g_hat_t - g||_inf and reconstruct g_hat_t by exactly this phase-averaged anchor-residual/absorption-weight formula, so both the interpretive claim and the experimental grounding rest on an unproven identity.

failure_location.quote: the true long-run average reward vector $g$ is invariant, meaning that time-averaging removes any peripheral components, and the projection of $g^\star$ onto $\ker(I-P)$ is $g$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a proposition in the justification section proving g = lim_T (1/T) sum_{t<T} P^t g* = Pi_{ker(I-P)} g* (equivalently g(s) = sum_i bar-theta_i p_i(s)), derived from eq:app_return_decomp_star together with the paper's own semisimplicity remark and cyclic Fourier decomposition of K(P), and connect it to the experimental reconstruction.
issues.overall_effect: The interpretation of the pipeline outputs as classical performance evaluation is unsupported: the link between the estimated objects ([v*], g*, theta*_{i,k}) and the actual evaluation target g is claimed but not established anywhere, and the experimental error metric and reconstruction lack theoretical justification.
issues.title: Claimed recovery of the classical average-reward vector g from the peripheral residual g* is asserted but never proved
issues.why_classification: The unsupported claim is central to the paper's stated evaluation guarantee and grounds the experiments, and repairing it requires a new, contained lemma (telescoping plus the semisimple Cesàro limit); since no content is lost and no global architecture is needed, this is more than minor but not serious.

issues.failure_explanation: For the unprojected iteration v_{t+1} = T(v_t) = r + Pv_t, the error with respect to the paper's gauge-fixed solution v* (which satisfies v* = Pi(r + Pv*), eq:proj_fixed_point) obeys e_{t+1} = Pe_t + g*, where g* = r + Pv* - v* is the peripheral residual, generally nonzero by Theorem thm:wellposed. In the paper's own two-state period-2 example both states are anchors, so v* = 0 and e_{t+1} = Pe_t + r, which differs from the claimed Pe_t whenever r != 0. The clean recurrence holds only for fixed points of T itself (zero-residual solutions), which for this chain need not exist in any gauge (they require r = 0 under the anchor gauge). The qualitative conclusion — the component along the eigenvector of -1 alternates and never contracts — survives, but the asserted error dynamics is false as written.

failure_location.quote: If $v_{t+1} = T(v_t)$ and $v^\star$ is any fixed point in a chosen gauge, then the error $e_t \coloneqq v_t - v^\star$ evolves as $e_{t+1} = P e_t$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the recurrence to e_{t+1} = Pe_t + g*, or analyze differences of iterates (v_{t+1} - v'_ {t+1} = P(v_t - v'_t)), noting that peripheral components do not contract.
issues.overall_effect: The stated mechanism for oscillation of naive fixed-point iteration on periodic chains is incorrect as written; the advertised phenomenon remains true and no labelled formal result relies on the erroneous recurrence.

issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction of the recurrence preserves the claim, its conclusion, and all downstream results; no new lemma, construction, or reoptimization is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof chain for thm:main_sa_rate (lem:projSA_stability_template, thm:projSA_rate_template, cor:optionB_rate) requires the uniform conditional second-moment bound eq:oracleB on the oracle noise along the iterates. For Algorithm 1's oracle, T_hat(v_t)(s) = r(s) + v_t(tilde s), this second moment is of order ||v_t||_inf^2, so the bound is equivalent to a priori boundedness of the iterates — exactly what the stability lemmas derive FROM the bound (lem:optionB_stability assumes the noise bound and concludes sup_t E||v_t||_inf^2 <= B_sup^2). The premise is therefore never established for the algorithm it is used about, and the main-text theorem does not even list it as a hypothesis (it appears only in the trailing clause on hidden constants). The formal end-to-end corollary cor:end_to_end_v likewise uses the constant sigma in its choice of T without assuming or verifying eq:oracleB for the pipeline. (The main-text statement also omits the stepsize schedule alpha_t = alpha/(t+t_0) with alpha(1-gamma_hat) > 1/2 that the formal proof requires.) A standard bootstrap argument closes the gap, but it is absent from the source.

failure_location.quote: where the hidden constants depend on the contraction parameters and the oracle second moment bound.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a bootstrap stability argument: bound the oracle noise by c||v_t||_inf^2 <= c'(||v*||_inf^2 + ||e_t||_q^2) on the anchored subspace W, insert this into the second-moment recursion, and choose t_0 large enough to absorb the resulting m_t term, yielding the uniform oracle bound and hence the stated rates for Algorithm 1; also state the oracle and stepsize conditions explicitly as hypotheses of thm:main_sa_rate and cor:main_end_to_end_v.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-sample convergence guarantee for Algorithm 1 and the advertised end-to-end query-complexity claims ('it suffices to choose K, T, M') are not established for the actual sampling scheme; all rates remain conditional on an unverified iterate-boundedness property.
